title: Closing Period of a Security Deposit Refund: Cash Earning Interest
content:
The cash on which a Security Deposit earns interest within a refund, for the closing period, depends on the refunds and payments among the deposit's transactions. The closing period runs from the period end of the latest interest credit on the deposit, or from the fully secured date when none has been credited, to the refund date.

| Deposit's transactions | Interest within the refund is earned on |
|---|---|
| An excess refund has been paid out of the deposit, and no deposit payment was received in the closing period | The cash received less the excess refunds paid |
| A deposit payment was received in the closing period | The cash held when the closing period began plus one half of the payments received in it |
| Neither | The cash received |

The cash received is the total of the deposit payments received on the deposit; an excess refund is a refund paid out of a held deposit after a recalculation lowered its required amount.

## Cases (hypothetical deposits)

1. Payments received USD 9000.00, all before the closing period; excess refund of USD 1500.00 paid earlier. Interest is earned on USD 7500.00.
2. Cash held USD 2000.00 when the closing period began, nothing refunded, and a USD 600.00 payment received during the period. Interest is earned on USD 2000.00 plus USD 300.00, that is USD 2300.00.
3. Payments received USD 480.00, nothing refunded and no payment in the closing period. Interest is earned on USD 480.00.
